note: Cases mirror event_wiring.rs: the orphan-listener, unused-emission (dead control, broadcast, stale, runtime-bound, imported-trait skips, external and config-knob exemptions) and unrouted-handler checks, each with a paired control. Every case carries the FIRED_HEARD and PRODUCED_HEARD answers of the program's helper traits. Expected findings are the code, path, message and suggestion the Rust validator reports for the same program.

findings.message: Trait 'C' listens for event 'GHOST' but no trait emits it
findings.suggestion: Ensure the event is emitted by another trait or remove the listener

findings.message: Trait 'P' emits event 'GO2' but no trait listens for it (nothing in this composition fires it, so this is a stale declaration rather than a dead control)
findings.suggestion: Consume it where it fires: add a transition arm `GO2 -> <state>` in the emitting trait (the usual pattern for persist/fetch success|failure events), declare the event `-> external` if a SIBLING orbital consumes it, or remove it from the emit config

findings.message: Trait 'T' emits event 'EV' but no trait listens for it — and a RENDERED control here fires it, so the affordance is dead and the value it carries is discarded
findings.suggestion: This trait is composed from an imported behavior, so THIS file is the consumer its `-> external` emit was declared for. Wire it at the call site: rename the event onto one you handle (`events { EV: <YOUR_EVENT> }`) and add a matching transition arm, or add `listens { T.EV -> <TRIGGER> }`. Re-declaring it `-> external` no longer suppresses this — that only defers an emit whose trait is DECLARED here.
